provenance.purpose: Curated disposition for NECB 2025 Section 8.4 articles that no gem manifest declares: who or what satisfies each one. Consumed by openstudio-necb/scripts/generate_necb_8_4_coverage.rb.

categories.engine: satisfied by EnergyPlus itself (physics the simulation engine performs)
categories.modeller: the modeller's or AHJ's responsibility — a scoping or input decision, not software
categories.covered_by: satisfied by named gem code that has not (yet) declared a manifest entry for this article
categories.gap: genuinely uncovered — nothing in the family satisfies it

provenance.rules: Every entry needs a rationale. A disposition is a claim of RESPONSIBILITY, not of correctness — the weaker claim is deliberate. Entries are drafts until a named human reviews them; the generator renders drafts distinctly and flags any article that is both dispositioned and declared/cited (conflicts are surfaced, never silently resolved).

8.4.1.3.rationale: The Part 3-7 Section .4 limitations are applicability conditions on using the performance path at all — a scoping judgement made before any software runs.

8.4.6.5.rationale: VERIFIED EQUIVALENT (Scroll + Reciprocating, water-cooled): CAP_FT, EIR_FPLR and EIR_FT all match at 0.00%. EIR_FT is compared against ERRATUM-CORRECTED coefficients: the PRINTED Table 8.4.5.5-C (2020) / 8.4.6.5-C (2025) rows carry single misplaced-decimal defects (Scroll d, Reciprocating b; the printed Reciprocating row yields a physically impossible negative power ratio at the AHRI rating point) — a publication error identical in both editions, NOT an extraction defect; errata proposed to NRC Codes Canada 2026-07-22. The corrections are corroborated EXACTLY by the independent legacy NECB-2011-lineage vendored curves (all six coefficients, <4e-6 relative, both rows). Screw/Centrifugal probed 2026-07-23 (D-13): all six curves EXACT vs the printed rows (not erratum-affected; their imperfect rating-point normalization is legacy-corroborated). probed by openstudio-necb/scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.rb.
8.4.6.5.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (batch review, probe-evidenced, openstudio-necb/docs/necb_decisions.md D-08)

8.4.6.6.rationale: The reference tower is CoolingTowerSingleSpeed: EnergyPlus computes available capacity with the Merkel effectiveness-NTU physical model, and the class has NO curve fields the FWB polynomial could be installed into. The FWB/FRA polynomial is the DOE-2.1E curve-fit of the SAME physics (identical coefficients in NECB 2020 8.4.5.6 / 2025 8.4.6.6; underlying relation tA = a + b.tR + c.tR2 + d.FRA + e.FRA2 + f.tR.FRA). NUMERIC CROSS-CHECK (rake necb:curves, gated): both formulations anchored at the CTI rating point (78F wb / 10F range / 7F approach) agree exactly there and within 12.7% across the CTI-wet-bulb slice; at colder wet-bulbs the code fit under-predicts available capacity relative to physics (conservative, up to ~2x at 50F wb) — precisely where capacity never binds because the single-speed fan cycles. E+ is the accepted stand-in for this same DOE-2 polynomial in every EnergyPlus-based 90.1 Appendix G tool. Note the reference tower's UA is sized at the builder's Canadian design point (24C wb / 5K approach / 6K range), a capacity-adequacy choice; 8.4.6.6 governs the part-load adjustment SHAPE, which the NTU model provides.
8.4.6.6.reviewer: phylroy — signed off 2026-07-23 (directed: disposition as engine, backed by the numeric FWB-vs-NTU cross-check)

The -10degC cutoff is separately applied per 8.4.5.13. probed 2026-07-22 (openstudio-necb/scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.rb).
